newsitem.title: USA: Militia leader urges McVeigh to demand execution.
newsitem.headline: Militia leader urges McVeigh to demand execution.

text.p: Norman Olson, who leads the Northern Michigan Regional Militia, Thursday urged Timothy McVeigh to demand that he be executed for killing 168 people in the Oklahoma City bombing.
"Targeting noncombatants is wrong and cannot be condoned by honourable men," Olson said in a statement released from his office in Alanson, Mich. "As a soldier, you must die for your war crime."

McVeigh, 29, was convicted Monday on all counts of blowing up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building. Before the April 19, 1995 explosion, McVeigh lived in Michigan with co-defendant Terry Nichols, who attended some militia meetings.

Olson, a Baptist minister and gun shop owner, was a co-founder of the Michigan Militia. He was ousted after he suggested the Oklahoma City bombing was a plot by foreign governments. He later formed the Northern Michigan Regional Militia.

Olson said he made his appeal to McVeigh in a letter sent through McVeigh's attorney, Stephen Jones. In his lengthy statement, Olson said McVeigh was "pushed beyond honour" by a corrupt U.S. government that abused its power during the Branch Davidian siege in Waco, Texas.
By accepting responsibility for the bombing, Olson said, McVeigh can send a message that actions have consequences.

"You will show that actions have consequences -- a message you attempted to convey to (Attorney General) Janet Reno and the mass murderers in the Justice Department who were absolved of wrongdoing following Waco," Olson wrote.
"Do the right thing now, Tim. Die for Janet Reno's sins for allowing Waco. Here is your chance to tell the world the true cause of your action. Let her forever live with that!"
